subject.title: [Feature]: Visible agent-to-agent messaging for ACP thread-bound sessions (proxy-only delivery without main session creation)

question: Which visible ACP-thread delivery contract should OpenClaw support for coordinator-to-worker instructions without creating main Discord session metadata?
rationale: The code can support more than one narrow fix shape, but choosing between a sessions_send API extension, a message proxy-only path, or an ACP-bound-thread exclusion rule changes public API semantics, upgrade behavior, and security boundaries.

options.title: Define Narrow Visible ACP Send
options.body: Add an explicit `sessions_send`-style visible delivery mode that is scoped to authorized ACP-bound sessions and proves no unintended main-session metadata is created.

options.title: Define Proxy-Only Message Send
options.body: Add a `message`/gateway send bypass for authorized proxy delivery, preserving normal outbound mirroring for every other send path.

options.title: Keep This Plugin-Owned
options.body: Decline a core API change and document a ClawHub/community relay path, accepting that current plugins cannot fully avoid the reported session-stub side effect.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Visible ACP Send
recommendation.body: Add an explicit `sessions_send`-style visible delivery mode that is scoped to authorized ACP-bound sessions and proves no unintended main-session metadata is created.

likelyOwner.reason: Most central current-main blame and shortlog history for the sessions_send, gateway schema, outbound metadata, and task delivery surfaces points to steipete as the strongest routing owner for the product/API choice.
